classes.plainDescription: A cholesterol pill used with or instead of a statin.

classes.plainDescription: An injection every 2 weeks to 6 months that strongly lowers LDL cholesterol.

records.verificationNote: Read directly from PDF p.38 (ANTILIPEMIC AGENTS). All listed statins are tier 1 with the PREV tag, which the formulary legend defines as a preventive drug required to be covered at no charge in select plans (PDF p.11). Atorvastatin 10/20/40/80 mg listed; 40 mg chosen as the mid-intensity preferred strength. Pitavastatin, fluvastatin, LIPITOR, CRESTOR, ZOCOR, and combinations (Vytorin, Roszet) are not listed. No PA or step (PDF p.6). Sig is standard label dosing, not printed in the document.

records.verificationNote: Read directly: ezetimibe tablets 10 mg tier 1, no QL or PA (PDF p.38). It is the only class member found, so the class-level answer is partial. Nexletol (bempedoic acid) and Nexlizet (bempedoic acid/ezetimibe) and ZETIA brand are not listed; absence is not confirmed exclusion because the formulary states it is not an all-inclusive list (PDF p.2). Fenofibrate, gemfibrozil, colestipol, and cholestyramine are tier 1 lipid agents outside this class definition and are not listed here.
